name: water_height_identity_swap
mechanism: Use three colored actual water-height spans and the corresponding top-view depth edges in B, swapping the identities of I and III. This invites the otherwise correct inverse-height reasoning to assign the greater depth to I instead of III. Roman numerals and gray water fill stay unchanged.
primary_math_proof: All three front widths are equal. A rectangular vase volume is front width times depth times water height. Water heights satisfy hII>hI>hIII. Because VI=VIII=4, depthIII>depthI. Also VII=3<4 and hII>hI, so depthII<depthI. Hence depthIII>depthI>depthII. Only A has that depth ordering. B reverses I and III; C,D,E fail the necessary ordering. Relative pixel heights are not treated as exact givens.

marker_roles.role: Front vase 1 left side below the original water surface: actual water-height span, not a new level.
Front vase 2 left side below the original water surface: actual water-height span, not a new level.
Front vase 3 left side below the original water surface: actual water-height span, not a new level.
B top view vase 1 depth edge: color-paired to source vase 3, swapping I/III while keeping II.
B top view vase 2 depth edge: color-paired to source vase 2, swapping I/III while keeping II.
B top view vase 3 depth edge: color-paired to source vase 1, swapping I/III while keeping II.
